evals.expected_output: Skill identifies GitLab as the host and loads its adapter, fetches MR metadata (including its pipeline status and author), compares the author against the authenticated user, searches for a work-item reference in the title/description, locates the local clone and creates an isolated review worktree detached at the MR's head SHA via the shared setup_worktree.py, hands the review to the review-changes skill (worktree path, base SHA as fixed point, work item file as spec, pipeline status as the test signal), posts each of its findings verbatim as an inline comment via scripts/post_review_notes_gitlab.py --mode direct (each ending with a 🤖), applies the verdict on the MR after the comments land, removes the worktree, and outputs the review in the conversation led by review-changes' verdict, including a 'Worth your own look' section naming Layer 1-2 files and an 'On the change' section stating what was posted, what the verdict did, and how to reverse it.
expectations: Skill identifies the host from the URL shape and reads references/hosts/gitlab.md before fetching anything

The review itself is delegated to the review-changes skill (invoked via the Skill tool), handed the worktree path, the base SHA as the fixed point, the saved work item file as the spec, and the host's checks status as the test signal — the skill does not re-derive the pyramid layers, severity split, or verdict itself

The isolated review worktree is created with the shared address-pr-comments/scripts/setup_worktree.py using --purpose review and --detach-sha <head_sha>, never by checking out the branch in the user's main clone
With no mode word after the URL, comments are published directly (--mode direct) rather than left as drafts
Comments are posted via scripts/post_review_notes_gitlab.py rather than hand-written glab api calls, and each one is marked with a 🤖 the script appends
No note attributing the review to a model is posted — the reviewing model's name and effort level appear nowhere on the MR
The verdict is acted on after the comments are published, never before: Approved or Approved with suggestions calls approve, Request changes does not
Approving passes sha=<head_sha> so a head that moved mid-review returns 409 and aborts the approval rather than approving a stale review

Inline comments default to 2-4 sentences of continuous prose (longer only for findings whose mechanism genuinely needs it, e.g. concurrency or security) and do not contain a separately labeled 'Failure scenario:' sub-paragraph

The conversation output leads with review-changes' verdict (Approved / Approved with suggestions / Request changes) and keeps its Requested changes, Suggestions, Checked and clean, and Path to merge sections, with each finding that was posted marked as such
The conversation output includes an 'On the change' section reporting what was posted, what the verdict action did, and the one-line way to reverse it

The conversation output includes a 'Worth your own look' section listing a short, selectively-chosen set of files (Layer 1 API Semantics and/or Layer 2 Implementation Semantics — new/changed public contracts or business-rule-bearing logic), with files sharing the same reason grouped into one line, and no note about what's lower priority
If a work item is found in the MR, it is saved to a file, handed to review-changes as the spec, and referenced in the output
review-changes' report is written to a file and not printed in the conversation — the only review the user reads is the skill's own final output
The run continues from the review straight into posting within the same turn: the comments and verdict land without the user having to ask whether they were published

Each comment is review-changes' report entry verbatim — layer tag and file:line citation included, only the list number stripped — never re-drafted, expanded, or re-explained for the MR; the citation is kept because a finding the host cannot anchor is re-posted positionless with the same text, and would otherwise name no location at all

A finding whose fix is an exact replacement of the line it anchors to carries a ```suggestion block in the note text, with the line's original indentation read from the worktree and no leading '+', so the author can apply it in one click — and no suggestion block is put on a general (unanchored) note

evals.prompt: Can you do a code review on https://gitlab.com/acme/platform/-/merge_requests/7? There's no ticket for this one, it's a quick hotfix.
evals.expected_output: Skill reviews the MR without work-item context: it tells review-changes there is no spec, and the conversation output carries review-changes' spec-less caveat — conformance was never assessed — alongside its verdict. Comments are published where issues exist and the verdict is recorded. Skill creates an isolated review worktree rather than checking out the branch in place.
expectations: The output states no work item was found and carries the spec-less caveat that conformance was not assessed
review-changes is invoked with no spec rather than the skill halting to ask for a work item
Comments are still published (review proceeds without work-item context) and the verdict is still recorded
Each comment carries the 🤖 marker the script appends and no model-attribution note is posted
The skill attempts to locate a local clone and create an isolated review worktree, or notes the diff-only limitation as a caveat

evals.prompt: Please review https://gitlab.com/acme/backend/-/merge_requests/201 — the ticket is GH-4521 in the MR title
evals.expected_output: Skill finds GH-4521 in the MR title, identifies it as a JIRA-style key, loads references/trackers/jira.md, fetches the work item, saves its summary/description/acceptance criteria verbatim to a file, and hands that path to review-changes as the spec so the report accounts for every requirement. The conversation output links to the work item.
expectations: Work item GH-4521 is fetched via the JIRA tracker adapter and referenced in the output
The fetched work item is written to a file and that path is passed to review-changes as the spec, rather than paraphrased into the prompt
The output accounts for the work item's requirements explicitly (each one satisfied, missing, partial, or wrong), and an unmet criterion is quoted verbatim in the inline comment that raises it
The review output is printed in the conversation and links to the work item
Nothing is posted back to the JIRA work item — the tracker adapter is read-only

evals.expected_output: Skill identifies GitHub as the host and loads references/hosts/github.md, fetches PR metadata via gh pr view (including author and statusCheckRollup), compares the author against gh api user, searches for a work-item reference, locates the local clone and creates an isolated review worktree detached at the PR's head SHA, hands the review to review-changes, publishes its findings via scripts/post_review_notes_github.py --mode direct (one comment call per anchored finding, conversation comments for unanchored ones, each ending with a 🤖), records the verdict as APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES after the comments land, removes the worktree, and outputs the verdict-led review in the conversation with an 'On the change' section.
expectations: Skill identifies GitHub as the host from the URL shape and reads references/hosts/github.md before fetching anything

The review itself is delegated to the review-changes skill (invoked via the Skill tool), handed the worktree path, the base SHA as the fixed point, the saved work item file as the spec, and the host's checks status as the test signal — the skill does not re-derive the pyramid layers, severity split, or verdict itself
Comments are posted via scripts/post_review_notes_github.py rather than hand-written gh api calls, and each one is marked with a 🤖 the script appends
No model-attribution text is posted — neither as a review body nor as a comment
A finding with no valid anchor is posted as a conversation comment on the PR rather than being dropped or pinned to an arbitrary line
The verdict is recorded after the comments are published: APPROVE carries no body, REQUEST_CHANGES carries the summary file GitHub requires for that event
The skill locates the clone by searching common roots and remote URL (never assuming one hardcoded clone root) and creates the review worktree beside it, or notes the diff-only limitation
The output's 'On the change' section names the verdict recorded and how to reverse it, referencing GitHub's own mechanics

A finding whose fix is an exact replacement of the line it anchors to carries a ```suggestion block in the inline comment, and a fix rewriting several existing lines is described in prose instead, since the bundled script anchors one line per comment

evals.prompt: Review https://github.com/acme/webapp/pull/88 — it's linked to issue acme/webapp#45
evals.expected_output: Skill identifies the work-item reference as a GitHub issue (not JIRA), loads references/trackers/github.md, fetches the issue via gh issue view, and uses its body as the requirements ground truth. The conversation summary links to the GitHub issue rather than a JIRA work item.
expectations: Skill correctly identifies the GitHub issue reference and loads the GitHub tracker adapter rather than the JIRA one
The GitHub issue is fetched, saved to a file, and handed to review-changes as the spec
The output accounts for the issue's stated requirements, or a comment references them
Nothing is posted to the issue itself — only to the PR

evals.expected_output: Skill recognizes the draft mode word, reviews the MR the same way, but leaves every finding as a GitLab draft note (no --mode direct) and takes no action on the MR's approval state. The output reports the verdict in the conversation and closes with GitLab's Submit review instruction.
expectations: The script is invoked without --mode direct, so findings stay as unpublished draft notes
No --verdict is passed and the MR's approval state is left untouched, even when the verdict is Approved
--purge is used so a rerun replaces this skill's own prior drafts rather than duplicating them
The output reports the verdict in the conversation and tells the user to open the MR and hit Submit review to publish the drafts

evals.expected_output: Skill publishes the comments directly but records no verdict: the script runs with --mode direct and --verdict none, so each finding lands as a standalone review comment (or a conversation comment when unanchored) and the PR's review state is untouched. The conversation output still leads with the verdict and says it was not recorded.
expectations: Comments are published directly rather than left as a pending review
No review event is submitted — no APPROVE, no REQUEST_CHANGES, and no review body carrying a summary
The output leads with review-changes' verdict and states explicitly that it was not recorded on the PR because comments-only mode was requested

evals.prompt: Review my own MR before I ask the team: https://gitlab.com/acme/my-service/-/merge_requests/61
evals.expected_output: Step 2 compares the MR's author against the authenticated user, finds they match, and drops to comments-only for the rest of the run: comments are published, no approve call is attempted, and the output explains that a self-authored change can't carry its author's verdict.
expectations: The skill compares the change's author against the authenticated user (glab api user / gh api user) as part of fetching metadata
On a match it does not attempt an approve call, rather than firing one and reporting the host's rejection
Comments are still published directly
The output states the verdict is informational because the change is self-authored

evals.prompt: Review https://gitlab.com/acme/backend/-/merge_requests/410 — I think it's broken, be strict
evals.expected_output: When review-changes returns Request changes, the skill writes the verdict line and summary paragraph to a summary file, runs the GitLab script with --mode direct --verdict request-changes --summary-file, and reports that GitLab exposes no API for a reviewer's requested-changes state — so the merge-blocking state needs a click in the UI.
expectations: A Request changes verdict passes --verdict request-changes with a --summary-file holding two or three sentences in the "I did not approve this merge request yet because <blocking finding>" shape — naming why it blocks and where the detail is, not restating the review's suggestions, checked-and-clean list, or path to merge
Any approval this account already holds on the MR is cleared (unapprove) rather than left standing under a Request changes verdict
The output tells the user that GitLab has no API for the requested-changes reviewer state and that setting it means opening the MR and choosing Request changes
The skill does not claim the MR is blocked from merging when only a comment and a cleared approval were applied
